title: Kelvin-Helmholtz swirls on the Sun’s surface
what: Time-lapse of the photosphere at 416 nm, the highest-resolution view of the Sun’s surface yet: magnetic-element edges curl into tiny whirlpools spaced about 50-65 km apart, with stripes tens of km wide.
licence: CC BY 4.0 per https://nso.edu/about/image-use-policy/ (credit must be visible, wording unaltered, linked online)

title: X1.3 flare and the thinnest coronal loops
what: H-alpha movie of an X1.3 flare’s decay on 2024-08-08, sped up 100x, about 4 Earth-diameters on a side: bright ribbons under hundreds of dark loops averaging 48 km wide, some perhaps 21 km.
licence: CC BY 4.0 per https://nso.edu/about/image-use-policy/ (credit must be visible, wording unaltered, linked online)

title: First sunspot
what: About 1.5 minutes of a sunspot on 2020-01-28 squeezed into a few seconds at 530 nm, about 12,000 miles across: penumbral grains and umbral dots shifting, with structures as small as 20 km.
licence: CC BY 4.0 per https://nso.edu/about/image-use-policy/ (credit must be visible, wording unaltered, linked online)
